info.title: Streamable Third-Party API
info.description:
Read-only access to ingests owned by the authorized Streamable user.

## Scopes

Scopes control the API permissions for an access token.
Each endpoint lists its required scopes.

During application creation, select the scopes that your integration needs.
An authorization request can include one or more approved scopes.
Separate multiple scopes with spaces in the `scope` parameter.
Request only the scopes required for your API calls.

| Scope | Access |
| --- | --- |
| `ingests:read` | Read owned ingests, publishing URLs, and stream keys. |

The examples in this guide call the ingest endpoints.
Therefore, they request `ingests:read`.
This table will list additional scopes when new API features require them.

## Authenticate

Streamable uses OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with S256 PKCE.

Create the authorization request and exchange the code on your server.
Keep the client secret, PKCE verifier, and all tokens on that server.

### 1. Create a Streamable application

1. Sign in to Streamable.
2. Open [Developer applications](https://streamable.run/developers/apps).
3. Select **Create application**.
4. Enter the app name, description, homepage, privacy policy, and terms URL.
5. Register each callback URI exactly.
6. Use HTTPS except for `localhost` or loopback development callbacks.
7. Do not use fragments or wildcards.
8. Select `ingests:read` for the ingest example in this guide.
9. Create the application.
10. When Streamable displays the client ID and client secret, save them in
    your server-side secret manager.
11. Wait until Streamable approves the application.

### 2. Start authorization

Use these values:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Authorization endpoint | `https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/auth` |
| Token endpoint | `https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/token` |
| API audience | `https://api.streamable.run/v1` |
| Scopes in this example | `ingests:read` |
| Response type | `code` |
| PKCE method | `S256` |
| Client authentication | HTTP Basic |

For each authorization attempt, complete these steps:

1. Generate `state` from 32 random bytes encoded as unpadded base64url.
2. Generate a PKCE verifier from 32 or more random bytes encoded as
   unpadded base64url.
3. Store both values in the server-side session for the browser.
4. Set the session to expire after 10 minutes.
5. Create `code_challenge` from the unpadded base64url encoding of
   `SHA-256(verifier)`.
6. Redirect the browser to this URL:

```text
https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/auth
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=<client_id>
  &redirect_uri=<exact_registered_callback>
  &scope=ingests%3Aread
  &audience=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.streamable.run%2Fv1
  &state=<single_use_random_state>
  &code_challenge=<s256_challenge>
  &code_challenge_method=S256
```

### 3. Process the callback

Streamable sends an HTTP `GET` request to the registered callback URI.

A successful callback contains `code` and `state`:

```http
GET /oauth/callback?code=<single_use_authorization_code>&state=<single_use_random_state> HTTP/1.1
Host: partner.example
```

An unsuccessful callback contains `error` and `state`:

```http
GET /oauth/callback?error=access_denied&error_description=<url_encoded_description>&state=<single_use_random_state> HTTP/1.1
Host: partner.example
```

For every callback, complete these steps:

1. Require the `state` parameter.
2. Compare `state` with the stored value by an exact, timing-safe comparison.
3. Reject a missing, different, expired, or previously used value.
4. Consume the stored authorization attempt.
5. If the callback contains `error`, stop the authorization flow.
6. Require the `code` parameter.
7. Exchange the code and PKCE verifier from your server:

```http
POST https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/token HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=authorization_code&code=<code>&redirect_uri=<exact_registered_callback>&code_verifier=<verifier>
```

Ignore unknown callback parameters.
Escape `error_description` before you display it.
Do not record the complete callback URL.

### Node.js example

This example requires Node.js 22 or later and a server-side session.

1. Set `STREAMABLE_CLIENT_ID` and `STREAMABLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the server environment.
2. Replace `redirectUri` with a registered callback URI.
3. Call `createAuthorizationUrl` from your authorization route.
4. Redirect the browser to the returned URL.
5. Call `exchangeCallback` from the registered callback route.
6. Store the returned tokens on your server.

```js
import { createHash, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

const clientId = process.env.STREAMABLE_CLIENT_ID;
const clientSecret = process.env.STREAMABLE_CLIENT_SECRET;
const redirectUri = "https://partner.example/oauth/callback";
const authorizationEndpoint = "https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/auth";
const tokenEndpoint = "https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/token";

if (!clientId || !clientSecret) {
  throw new Error("Missing Streamable OAuth credentials.");
}

function formEncode(value) {
  return new URLSearchParams({ value }).toString().slice("value=".length);
}

function basicClientAuthorization() {
  const credentials = `${formEncode(clientId)}:${formEncode(clientSecret)}`;
  return `Basic ${Buffer.from(credentials).toString("base64")}`;
}

function matchesState(expectedState, suppliedState) {
  const expected = Buffer.from(expectedState);
  const supplied = Buffer.from(suppliedState ?? "");
  return (
    expected.length === supplied.length &&
    timingSafeEqual(expected, supplied)
  );
}

export function createAuthorizationUrl(session) {
  const state = randomBytes(32).toString("base64url");
  const verifier = randomBytes(64).toString("base64url");
  const challenge = createHash("sha256")
    .update(verifier)
    .digest("base64url");

  // Store this only in a short-lived server-side session.
  session.streamableOAuth = {
    state,
    verifier,
    expiresAt: Date.now() + 10 * 60 * 1_000,
  };

  const url = new URL(authorizationEndpoint);
  url.search = new URLSearchParams({
    response_type: "code",
    client_id: clientId,
    redirect_uri: redirectUri,
    scope: "ingests:read",
    audience: "https://api.streamable.run/v1",
    state,
    code_challenge: challenge,
    code_challenge_method: "S256",
  }).toString();
  return url.toString();
}

export async function exchangeCallback(callbackUrl, session) {
  const callback = new URL(callbackUrl, redirectUri);
  const attempt = session.streamableOAuth;

  if (
    !attempt ||
    attempt.expiresAt < Date.now() ||
    !matchesState(attempt.state, callback.searchParams.get("state"))
  ) {
    throw new Error("The OAuth callback state is invalid or expired.");
  }
  delete session.streamableOAuth; // Consume the validated attempt once.

  if (callback.searchParams.has("error")) {
    throw new Error("Streamable authorization was not completed.");
  }
  const code = callback.searchParams.get("code");
  if (!code) throw new Error("The OAuth callback is missing its code.");

  const response = await fetch(tokenEndpoint, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Accept: "application/json",
      Authorization: basicClientAuthorization(),
      "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    },
    body: new URLSearchParams({
      grant_type: "authorization_code",
      code,
      redirect_uri: redirectUri,
      code_verifier: attempt.verifier,
    }),
  });
  const tokens = await response.json().catch(() => null);
  if (
    !response.ok ||
    typeof tokens?.access_token !== "string" ||
    typeof tokens?.refresh_token !== "string"
  ) {
    throw new Error("The authorization-code exchange failed.");
  }
  return tokens;
}
```

Use `expires_in` to set the access-token expiration time.
Do not inspect the token format.

### 4. Call the API

Send the access token as an HTTP bearer credential:

```http
GET https://api.streamable.run/v1/ingests HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Accept: application/json
```

The token must grant `ingests:read`.
The user must have an active Streamable subscription.
A successful response contains the user's publishing credentials.
The response uses `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

### 5. Refresh the access token

Each authorization-code exchange returns an access token and a rotating refresh token.
Send the stored refresh token to get new tokens:

```http
POST https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/token HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=<refresh_token>
```

After each successful refresh, replace both stored tokens in one operation.
Do not reuse the old refresh token.

### 6. Revoke tokens

When a user disconnects the app, revoke the access token:

```http
POST https://auth.streamable.run/oauth2/revoke HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=<access_token>&token_type_hint=access_token
```

Then revoke the refresh token with `token_type_hint=refresh_token`.
Delete all stored copies after both requests.

Revocation succeeds if the token is already inactive.
Access-token revocation can take up to 30 seconds to reach the API.

### 7. Protect credentials

Do not record these values in browser code, URLs, logs, analytics, traces,
crash reports, or shared caches:

- Client secrets
- Access tokens and refresh tokens
- Authorization codes and PKCE values
- Response bodies
- Stream keys and complete publishing URLs

Store `X-Request-Id` for support.

get.summary: List the authorized user's owned ingests
get.description: Returns every ingest owned directly by the token subject, up to the product's bounded ingest limit. Publishing credentials are included in successful responses, which are always marked private and no-store.

200.description: All owned ingests within the product's bounded ingest limit.

get.description: Returns one ingest only when it is owned directly by the token subject. A missing ingest and an ingest owned by another user produce the same not-found response.

200.description: The owned ingest and its publishing endpoints.

oauthAccessToken.description: Opaque access token issued by Streamable OAuth.

scopes.ingests:read: Read owned ingests, publishing URLs, and stream keys.

CacheControl.description: Credential-bearing responses are private and must not be stored.

RequestId.description: Correlation identifier for support and incident investigation.

WwwAuthenticate.description: OAuth bearer-token challenge for token or scope failures.

url.description: RTMP publishing URL, including the application path.
SRT publishing URL without credential-bearing query parameters.
SRTLA regional relay URL without credential-bearing query parameters.

InvalidToken.description: The token is missing, invalid, expired, revoked, or not valid for this API.

Forbidden.description: Insufficient scope or an active Streamable subscription is required.

NotFound.description: The ingest is missing or is not owned by the token subject.

Unavailable.description: A required service is temporarily unavailable.
